Building HomeView/CaptureRootView now would mean coding against types (WorkoutSession, ExerciseRuleEngine, etc.) that don't exist as real files yet — premature and likely to churn.

**Flagging for the integrator / other lanes:**
1. There's still no `.xcodeproj`/App entry anywhere in `app_build` — that's the integrator's lane, but it's the actual blocker for anything to compile. Worth prioritizing so Milestone 0's tests can actually run.
2. I renamed the scaffold's `DS` enum to `Theme` — safe now since nothing referenced `DS.*` yet, but flagging loudly so nobody builds against the old name from stale context.
3. Hex values in `Theme.Colors` are my own reasonable stand-ins for the "quiet spotter" mood (muted slate-blue accent, warm amber pair) — not lifted from a pixel-exact design_handoff artifact I don't have direct file access to. If a real token sheet exists elsewhere, swap these in; otherwise these are the values screens should build against.
4. Everything downstream (HomeView, CaptureRootView, HistoryView, SettingsView, KnownLimitsView, Theme consumers) should route through `Theme.*` now — I'll pick those up once Milestone 0's core types land and the wave gate opens.

**What remains:** all of primary_ui's actual screens (nothing to build them against yet), plus reconciling the flows.json accessibility-identifier tokens (`home.demoSessionToggle`, `capture.classifierChip`, `capture.classifierOption.pushUp`, etc.) into those screens once they exist.

Built out my lane's foundational pieces for this round — the things other lanes will need to wire into once their types land, since data_domain's `WorkoutSession`/`SessionRepository`/`ExerciseKind` and primary_ui's `CaptureSessionModel` aren't in the tree yet this same parallel round.

**Files created:**
- `Features/KnownLimits/CapabilityGap.swift` — `CapabilityGap`/`GapCategory` exactly per the interface contract.
- `Features/KnownLimits/KnownLimitsStore.swift` — `@MainActor @Observable KnownLimitsStore`, pre-seeded at init with the HealthKit-presumed-blocked gap ([REDACTED:high_entropy]). Kept `record(_:)` to the exact contracted signature but made it dedupe by category+title so repeated capability checks (e.g. Home re-checking camera status on every appear) don't spam duplicate rows. Added `replaceGaps(in:with:)` and `clearGaps(in:)` as additive helpers — these are what closes [REDACTED:high_entropy]: whichever service owns the real `HKHealthStore` authorization call needs a way to retract the pre-seeded "blocked" entry once it observes a real outcome, and the bare `record` alone can't do that (it can only add/overwrite, not remove). Flagging this for whoever builds T-010 (HealthKitWriting) — call `replaceGaps(in: .healthKit, with: nil)` on success, or `replaceGaps(in: .healthKit, with:)` a fresh gap on a *real* denial, so the app's own honesty screen never stays wrong after a real authorization attempt.
- `Features/Reconciliation/SessionReconciliationService.swift` — `reconcileOrphanedSessions(in:)`, fetches all sessions (`includeDemo: true`, since a demo playback interrupted mid-fixture deserves the same honest treatment) and finalizes any `.inProgress`/`.finalizing` orphan as ended-early, per DEC-tech_specs-008.
- `Features/Accessibility/AccessibilityAnnouncer.swift` — posts `AccessibilityNotification.Announcement` directly for rep count and form flags, not label-diffing, per DEC-design_handoff-007.
- `Features/Resilience/InterruptionCoordinator.swift` — observes `AVCaptureSession.wasInterruptedNotification`, hops to `@MainActor`, and calls `model.endSet()` only if actually `.inSession` (guards against double-ending after a clean finish), per [REDACTED:high_entropy].
- `Tests/KnownLimitsStoreTests.swift` — real Swift Testing coverage of pre-seeding, record/dedupe, replace, and clear, since `KnownLimitsStore` is the one piece in my lane with zero external-lane dependencies and could be tested standalone right now.

**What works now:** `KnownLimitsStore` is fully self-contained and correct as written — I couldn't run the compiler in this sandbox (xcrun/swiftc calls need an approval I can't grant myself here), so I hand-verified syntax/types carefully instead of claiming a build I didn't observe. The other four files are written exactly against interfaces.json's signatures but reference types (`WorkoutSession`, `SessionRepository`, `CaptureSessionModel`, `FormFlagRecord`, `ExerciseKind`) owned by data_domain/primary_ui that aren't in the tree yet this round, so they can't compile standalone until those land.

**What's left for the integrator:** register these new files into the app/test target membership (I didn't touch Package.swift/pbxproj per my lane boundary); confirm the test target's module name — I guessed `@testable import Formcheck` per DEC-task_assignments-001, flag if that's wrong; once `CaptureSessionModel` exists, `InterruptionCoordinator` needs to actually be instantiated and wired to the live `AVCaptureSession` somewhere in the capture pipeline (that call site belongs to primary_ui/services_utilities, not me); once `HealthKitWriting` exists, its owner should call `KnownLimitsStore.replaceGaps(in: .healthKit, ...)` on the real auth outcome as noted above. `SessionReconciliationService` also needs to actually get invoked at app launch before History/Watch/Catalyst read the store — that's the integrator's `@main App` init, outside my lane.
